themes.theme: Private Rented Sector Context and Regulation
themes.reason: Provides background scale and regulatory context for the sector but does not itself explain why fees are high or opaque; sets the stage rather than carrying the argument.

themes.theme: Letting Agent Fees Charged to Tenants
themes.reason: This is the central evidence establishing that tenant fees are high, variable, hard to compare and inconsistently charged, directly substantiating the diagnosis of high, opaque fees.

themes.theme: Letting Agent Fees Charged to Landlords
themes.reason: Provides a contrast showing landlord fees are more transparent and market-based, but is supporting/comparative detail rather than a main pillar of the diagnosis.
Demonstrates directly that fees are opaque despite legal requirements and that some agents engage in unfair practices, core to the 'opaque' part of the diagnosis.
Explains the causal mechanism—weak competitive pressure and misaligned incentives—for why fees are high and opaque, a core explanatory pillar of the diagnosis.

themes.theme: Financial Impact on Tenants and Tenancy Churn
themes.reason: Shows the scale and real-world harm of high fees (financial strain, repeated charges), central to establishing why the high fees are a problem worth addressing.
Contains unrelated or marginal remarks (discrimination against benefit claimants, Northern Ireland surveys) that are not integral to the core diagnosis argument.
